summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and a history of recurrent atrial tachycardia was admitted after developing palpitations with a heart rate of 120–130 during dialysis, following fluid removal and withholding of metoprolol. She was hypotensive initially but responded to fluid resuscitation. Workup showed no myocardial infarction, with stable troponins and no growth on blood cultures. An echocardiogram revealed diastolic dysfunction and moderate pulmonary hypertension without significant change from prior. The electrophysiology team recommended transitioning from diltiazem and metoprolol to amiodarone to avoid hypotension and better control arrhythmias. Warfarin was adjusted to 1 mg daily due to interaction with amiodarone. She remained stable, completed a hemodialysis session, and was discharged to extended care with updated medications and close follow-up plans.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
